brief: The canvas presents a colossal cross-section of Earth's history, depicting deeply saturated layers of mineral deposits and striated rock strata. Massive bands of color—ranging from oxidized reds and ochres to deep, cool greens—overlap and bleed into one another, suggesting immense geologic time. The composition appears to flow and change autonomously, as if the canyon wall is constantly undergoing slow, relentless erosion. The viewer observes the slow shifting of these massive, beautiful geological planes, watching the visible processes of uplift and decay play out across the simulated scale of an immense natural canyon.

statement: This sketch depicts a vast geological cross-section of Earth's history, rendered as flowing layers of mineral deposits and eroded rock strata. Through the slow, autonomous motion of these layers—simulating uplift and decay—viewers witness an abstracted yet vivid representation of immense geologic time. The composition uses deeply saturated colors and subtle animations to evoke the feeling of a canyon wall in constant, slow transformation. The viewer observes a continuous, mesmerizing interplay of color, form, and motion that suggests both the violence and patience inherent in natural processes.
